summary.headline: Kirloskar Ferrous Q2 FY27 revenue rose 16% YoY to Rs 2,057 crore, while PBT of Rs 138 crore was held back by tube margin pressure and casting rejections.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 topline was Rs 2,057 crore versus Rs 1,755 crore a year earlier (+16%), with PBT of Rs 138 crore against Rs 120 crore. Casting sales of Rs 633 crore (+30%) and pig iron of Rs 581 crore (+20%) led growth, while tubes grew only 0.5%. Realisations rose across pig iron (+12.4%), castings (+6.8%), steel (+7.6%) and tubes (+1.6%), though management said margins remain under pressure in castings and tubes. Management flagged a casting rejection problem at Solapur and an expected tractor-segment slowdown.

financial_highlights.change: vs Rs 120 crore a year earlier

financial_highlights.metric: H1 pig iron hot metal production

segments.name: Pig iron
segments.commentary: Sales value Rs 581 crore (+20% YoY); external pig iron volume about 1,34,000 t vs 1,28,000 t (+3.5%). One export cargo of 31,000 t was shipped at better realisation than domestic. Realisation Rs 43,054/t (+12.4%).

segments.name: Castings
segments.commentary: Sales value Rs 633 crore (+30%); gross casting sales crossed 50,000 t for the first time, net sales 47,888 t (+20%). Realisation Rs 1,30,000/t (+6.8%). Solapur about 15,000 t/quarter; Rajpura about 6,000 t+ in a quarter.

segments.name: Steel
segments.commentary: External steel sales Rs 206 crore (+48% YoY); realisation Rs 77,500/t (+7.6%). Steel production H1 up about 14%.

segments.name: Tubes
segments.commentary: Sales growth only 0.5% in value; volume 48,547 t (about -2%). Realisation +1.6%. Management said margins are under pressure, with Q1 volumes weak on delayed oil and gas projects.

guidance_outlook: Tube volumes targeted above 1,00,000 t in H2 FY27 to show growth over last year.
Casting net sales targeted to stabilise at about 1 lakh t in each of the next two quarters; management said casting capacity and rejections are being addressed to reach this level.
Solapur utilisation to rise to 6,000 t/month (18,000 t/quarter) across both foundries, with a 70,000 t/annum target for Solapur.
Pig iron domestic volume expected to be better than last year, at about 6.6-6.7 lakh t; oxygen enrichment and PCI at Koppal blast furnaces 1 and 2 due by year-end.
Medium-term target of 15% volume growth per year in castings; long-term pig iron sales target of 0.5 million t.
Machining value to cross Rs 100 crore annually within a year or two, with about 60% expected as contribution.
capex_capacity: Solapur second foundry line (two-part/no-bake, large castings up to 2 t): phase one and two nearly complete; commissioning expected by January 2027; total foundry capacity 15,000 t/annum (1,250 t/month).
Rajpura phase two targeted by March 2027 to take capacity to about 4,000 t/month; phase three needed for 70,000 t/annum; Rajpura stabilised at about 2,200 t/month with rejections falling.
Koppal alloy steel plant: technology partners engaged; equipment ordering and commercial negotiation under way; about 20 months execution after a 2-3 month start.
Jejuri rolling mill expansion, Baramati expander mill and Ahmednagar small piercing mills: execution stage; timelines not specified.
Machining capex about Rs 200 crore to date (per management correction from Rs 240 crore); annual machining value about Rs 50-60 crore (about Rs 5 crore/month).
Only 35 MW of wind power commissioned at Solapur; other windmills not yet commissioned.
Hiriyur mini-blast furnace upgrade planned; all three mini-blast furnaces together could give 8.5-9 lakh t of pig iron output before conversion to steel.
demand_pricing: Casting demand strong from automotive, earth-moving and stationary engine segments; foundries fully loaded in Q2 and October. Management flagged possible small corrections in tractor demand.
Casting contracts use a quarter-on-quarter price pass-through, so some further price increases are still to be realised.
Pig iron is priced on a monthly spot basis; coking coal is the main cost driver, while iron ore costs have been broadly stable.
Tube demand held back by delayed oil and gas projects; Chinese dumping expected to ease after anti-dumping duty was extended for five years; US exports hit by the war situation.
Pig iron exports were uneconomic for internal plants at current prices, per management; export opportunities will be taken only occasionally.
Rejections at Solapur about 10-11%, expected to fall to 7-8% next quarter; Rajpura rejections expected below 5%.

qa_highlights.question: Is Solapur phase two demand visible, and where is the Jejuri steel project and the Koppal alloy steel plant?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Solapur phase one and two are nearly complete and ramping up (about 15,000 t/quarter). Koppal alloy steel ordering is under way, with about 20 months of execution after a 2-3 month start. Jejuri and other projects have seen delays but are in execution.

qa_highlights.question: Why did casting margins contract despite higher volume and realisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited quarterly price pass-through lags, unfinished windmill commissioning, and productivity and quality work still needed. Further price realisation is expected in coming quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Was pig iron export a conscious choice, and what is the domestic run rate?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the export cargo was a short window of better prices that also eased domestic pressure. Volume is expected to be about 6.6-6.7 lakh t, rising as Koppal oxygen enrichment and PCI are added.

qa_highlights.question: How much casting volume will the large-casting line add in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects no meaningful volume in FY27, with meaningful volume in FY28 as some parts move from makeshift arrangements to formal production.

qa_highlights.question: Why are tube volumes flat and margins down?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q1 was weak because oil and gas projects were delayed, and Q2 margins were still under pressure from low-priced orders. Realisation improvement is expected from new orders, with one large export consignment slipping into Q3.

qa_highlights.question: Why is machining revenue low relative to investment?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said machining capex is about Rs 200 crore and revenue is about Rs 50-60 crore a year; the gap reflects customer model changes and infrastructure. Target is Rs 100 crore within a year or two, with customer co-investment and special-purpose machines.

qa_highlights.question: Is casting capacity sufficient for customer demand, and what is the rejection trend?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said customer commitments exceed 3 lakh t per annum, so new capacity or acquisitions are being evaluated. Solapur rejections are expected to fall to 7-8% from 10-11% next quarter.

risks_watch: Casting gross-to-net gap: rejections of about 3-4% and Solapur thin-wall rejections at 10-11% need to fall as guided.
Tube margins and volumes: H2 target of over 1 lakh t depends on oil and gas project execution, with Chinese imports and weak US exports as headwinds.
Tractor segment demand softening, which management flagged as a possible risk to casting volumes.
Machining utilisation: customer model changes have led to 50-60% of capacity being bought, against the Rs 100 crore target.
Management succession: leadership transition is in progress with no timelines disclosed.
Project execution timelines: Koppal alloy steel (about 20 months from order), Jejuri rolling mill and Rajpura phase two (by March 2027) may slip.
summary.management_tone: Confident on top-line growth, pricing and casting demand, but cautious on tube margins, casting rejections and project timelines. Management repeatedly qualified targets with 'hopeful' and 'quite optimistic' language and avoided committing to pig iron price direction.
key_quotes: So, it looks like we have come out of the low commodity cycle, gradually going up.
I am quite hopeful, confident that this change will come and we will see further improvement in the tube.
Total foundry capacity would be 15,000 metric tons per annum.
And we will continue to focus and continue to grow on the casting volumes in coming years because we have lined up new customer additions as well as the existing customers.
